posts.author: Hans
posts.content_md:
Does anyone have experience with the Russian GP-2 and GP-3 developers? I like the idea of not having a part A+B developer. You can make the developer in one batch and it seems to keep good with time. When it needs to be used, mix 15ml of the stock developer with 400ml of water and use it.

I don't have the necessary chemicals in house for making it, but if it works well, I would like to try it.

[http://holography.ru/les10eng.htm](http://holography.ru/les10eng.htm)

posts.author: Hans
posts.content_md: Ah, and I forgot to mention that this developer bleaches the film at the same time as during development.

posts.author: al_gont
posts.content_md:
I always use GP-3. It works well. 

I don't know about GP-2, but GP-3 keeps good for a month or so. After that it becomes yellow because of oxidation. It still works, but I prefer to mix another portion of developer than to wait untill it doesn't 

I tried 15/400 but it turned to be too strong and the plate became too dark after needed 5 minutes. So I reduced the ratio to 12/400. Now everything is ok. I guess the ratio may differ due to quality of chemicals or something like this.

You are not quite right about bleaching. GP-3 doesn't bleach plate/film.

posts.author: Martin
posts.content_md:
> **Hans:** Ah, and I forgot to mention that this developer bleaches the film at the same time as during development.

The stock solutions of those colloidal developers keep pretty well. 

Colloidal development forms an amplitude and phase hologram at the same time. So such developers don't bleach the emulsion actually. Upon development tiny disc shaped silver particles are generated, resulting in (yellow-red) colloidal layers.

posts.author: Hans
posts.content_md: Can GP-3 be used for both transmission and reflection work? From what I understand so far, it seems to be an ideal developer for someone who likes to make a hologram every evening.

posts.author: Martin
posts.content_md:
> **Hans:** Can GP-3 be used for both transmission and reflection work? From what I understand so far, it seems to be an ideal developer for someone who likes to make a hologram every evening.

For transmission gratings we've never had good results with the GP developers.

Solution-physical (colloidal) development requires higher exposure levels than chemical development.

posts.author: al_gont
posts.content_md:
The matter is not in the type of hologram but in the size of grains of recording material.

GP-3 is to be used for PFG-03m. It won't work with VPR or PFG-01 that are usually used for recording transmission holograms.

In fact, transmission hologram can be recorded on PFG-03m. It is about ten times less sensitive and exposure will take much more time. But it can be proccessed with GP-3.
